answer.evidence: The cell is a flat, full-width 16x16 tile. Rows 0-1 are a 2-row brown strip with no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so it works as a rim at most. Rows 2-4 are a cream face-on band. Row 5 is a dark outline around a window inset, and rows 6-14 are the window (white frame, blue glass, pale sill). The tile shows no sloped roof plane, ellipse, or visible contents. Every part is a vertical face, so there is no real top surface and it matches the 'rim only' and 'front elevation' reference examples.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single 16x16-sized icon: a pale frame around a blue panel, like a window or sign. It has no roof, walls or door, so it is not a whole building like the two references, which have scalloped tile roofs with per-tile highlights, plaster speckle, timber or stone shading and doors. The measured facts are comparable to the references (11 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 0% near-flat coverage, 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges are tinted). That does not offset the structural gap. By eye it shows only about 3 lightness steps on its materials, against 5-6 on the references, and it carries far less shape and grain information at building scale. A careful artist would not accept it as a building next to these references.
